result:
The binade rule predicts the second geometry exactly. PR #376 is marked ready; CI on the final push had not reported when I stopped.

**What I tested.** The `Texture_render_target` quad has the same vertex order as the checkerboard. Row 240 sits at l2 = 1/2 exactly. There the rule reduces to "in the upper-right triangle, down iff l0 ≤ 1/4", which puts the switch at column 392. I committed that prediction (`d0e6d4cd54`) before running the scorer.

**Score** (40 goldens, `6e159f1`, 2026-08-11):

| rule | agrees / observable tie px |
|---|---:|
| binade rule | 6,108 / 6,108 (100%) |
| edge-function binade (down from column 406) | 95.35% |
| always up (what we render today) | 75.88% |
| checkerboard split carried over in screen space (x ≥ 481) | 75.88% |
| #314 diagonal rule | 75.46% |

Every capture that can show the switch has it between columns 391 and 392. The console set (2026-09-25) is byte-identical to the goldens again, so it adds no independent sample.

**Limits on what this shows:**
- It confirms the rule is keyed on the barycentric weights, not on screen position or edge-function size. It only exercises the l2 = 1/2 condition, which is also the checkerboard's row 240. The rule's other conditions are still checked only on the checkerboard.
- It is not a blind test. `render-to-texture-residual.md` already recorded that our output differs at columns 392–462, and I had read that before deriving the prediction. The rule has no free parameter to tune, and the NOTES say this up front.

**It corrects two earlier readings:**
- `render-to-texture-residual.md` calls row 240 "wholly shifted" with 214 columns unobservable. On the 15 formats that carry a gradient in every column, all 285 columns are observable: 214 go up and 71 go down.
- cloud-282b said the rule can't be implemented without a fragment-barycentric extension. psh.c already gets the three vertex positions for every triangle draw (`geom.c:236-238`) and computes the weights from them in the depth path (`psh.c:2604-2615`). The only missing input is each vertex's texcoords.

**Recommendation: a scoped code lane.** It would pass each vertex's texcoords from `glsl/geom.c` (held by lane.vkpointsize34) and make the v sign of `texelTieBias` in `glsl/psh.c` per-pixel (held by lane.fog278). It should cover only the measured case and keep today's "up" everywhere else. The general rule for arbitrary texcoords isn't determined by any data on disk: the obvious generalisation fails on the lower-left triangle's u ties. The recoverable pixels are all from synthetic test patterns, so this ranks below suites with residuals games can show.

For #286 (lane.aasample), the "texel 2x+1" answer stands. Row 240 is a v tie on the fixed-function path, so it adds nothing new about the resolve's u tie. I said so on #286 and posted the result on #282.

The write-up is in `docs/lanes/tie282c/NOTES.md`, with `row240.py` to reproduce the table; preflight passed.
